title: Maintenance Simulation & Field Drill
contentStatus: Built per Content Principles (60% pass, terminology + notes). This is the capstone module for L3A - a new module per CDD (does not exist in DiFacto's original slide deck), designed as performance-under-time-pressure assessment, the Technician-track equivalent of ITA's 'Applied' certification tier. Lab/drill logistics pending DiFacto facility confirmation.

sections.title: Why This Module Exists
learningObjectives: Understand the purpose of a timed field drill as a capstone assessment
Recognize the difference between knowing procedures and performing them under pressure
sections.content: Modules 1 through 6 built the knowledge base - diagnostic methodology, maintenance procedures, battery health, root cause analysis. This module tests whether that knowledge holds up under realistic conditions: time pressure, an unfamiliar fault presentation, and the expectation of working independently. This is what distinguishes a certified Technician from someone who has only studied the material.

keyTerms.note: A robot that navigates autonomously using sensor-based awareness of its surroundings — the category MoRo belongs to.

sections.title: Drill Structure
learningObjectives: Understand the general format of the field drill
Know what's being assessed beyond the final fix
sections.content: The drill presents a realistic fault scenario on an actual or simulated MoRo unit, with a defined time window to diagnose and resolve it. Assessment isn't limited to whether the fix is correct - the approach matters too: did you follow structured diagnostic methodology (from L3A-M5), did you document appropriately, did you make the correct call on whether the issue was within field-serviceable scope or required escalation. Exact drill scenarios and facility requirements are being finalized with DiFacto's operations team.

sections.title: Working Under Time Pressure
learningObjectives: Understand how time pressure affects diagnostic work
Know strategies for maintaining structured methodology under a deadline
sections.content: Time pressure tends to push people toward guessing rather than systematic diagnosis - jumping to a likely-looking cause instead of confirming the category first. The discipline this drill reinforces: even under a clock, start broad and narrow systematically. A fast wrong diagnosis costs more time than a methodical correct one, since a wrong fix often means starting over.

sections.title: Working Independently
learningObjectives: Understand the shift from guided learning to independent performance
Recognize when independent judgment calls for escalation versus continued attempt
sections.content: Unlike earlier modules, this drill is performed without step-by-step guidance - reflecting what actual field conditions require. Part of what's being assessed is judgment: knowing when to keep working a diagnosis versus recognizing it's outside field-serviceable scope and should be escalated, per the criteria covered in L3A-M5.

sections.title: Safety Under Pressure
learningObjectives: Understand that safety protocols don't relax under time pressure
Recognize this as part of the assessment criteria, not a separate concern
sections.content: Time pressure is never a justification for skipping safety procedures - lockout/tagout before physical maintenance work, proper E-stop usage during testing, careful handling around powered systems. This is assessed as part of the drill, not treated separately: a technically correct fix achieved by bypassing safety procedure does not pass.

sections.title: Completing L3A Certification
learningObjectives: Understand how this module completes the L3A certification requirement
Recognize what DiFacto Certified IMR Technician status represents
sections.content: Successfully completing this drill, alongside the written and practical components of Modules 1 through 6, completes the requirements for DiFacto Certified IMR Technician status. This certification represents verified competency, not just completed coursework - the field drill exists specifically to make that distinction real.

questions.question: What does this module primarily assess, beyond whether the final fix is correct?
options: Whether structured methodology, documentation, and escalation judgment were applied
How fast the technician can work regardless of approach
Nothing else matters besides the final fix
questions.feedback: Correct. Approach and judgment are assessed alongside the outcome, not just the final result.

questions.question: How does time pressure typically affect diagnostic work if not managed deliberately?
options: It tends to push toward guessing rather than systematic diagnosis
It has no effect on diagnostic approach
questions.feedback: Correct. Time pressure can push toward shortcuts; maintaining structured methodology under pressure is the skill being tested.

questions.question: Is this drill performed with step-by-step guidance?
options: Only the first attempt is unguided
No - it's performed independently, reflecting real field conditions
questions.feedback: Correct. Independent performance is central to what this module assesses.

questions.question: Does time pressure justify skipping safety procedures during the drill?
options: No - safety procedures are assessed as part of the drill, not relaxed under pressure
Yes, if it saves significant time
questions.feedback: Correct. A technically correct fix that bypasses safety procedure does not pass.

questions.question: What does completing this module alongside Modules 1-6 achieve?
options: Nothing formal - it's an optional exercise
Completion of the requirements for DiFacto Certified IMR Technician status
questions.feedback: Correct. This drill is the capstone requirement completing L3A Technician certification.
